properties.name: Grok becomes its own harness and gets the TOML config it actually reads
properties.rationale: THE BELIEF WAS NEVER MEASURED AND A USER PAID FOR IT. The alias was added 2026-08-14 on learning that the second user runs Grok at home and Claude at work — a fact about the PERSON. The config-location claim rode along with it, and the file then asserted for a month that Grok CLI loads .mcp.json as a compatibility source. Measured 2026-09-20 against Grok Build 1.0.30: `grok mcp list`, run inside a project holding a valid reflow2 .mcp.json, answers "No MCP servers configured", and `grok mcp add --help` names its only two sources, ~/.grok/config.toml and ./.grok/config.toml. So answering "grok" produced .reflow2/, a pointer file, and a config the tool never opens — which presents to the agent as reflow2 not being registered for the project, which is exactly how it was reported. THE STANDARD WAS ALREADY IN THE FILE, TWELVE LINES BELOW. The Copilot alias records that product's own help output and an end-to-end confirmation with `copilot mcp list`. One claim was measured and its neighbour was assumed, in the same block, in the same week. So the class is that reflow2 asserts where other products keep their MCP configuration, one product at a time, with no check — and a fix that only adds a grok entry leaves the next client to be guessed at. WHAT IS NOT BUILT AND WHY: a gate that runs each product's own list command inside a freshly installed directory cannot run in CI, where those binaries are absent. The honest form is a local instrument plus a recorded per-client measurement date, in the shape check_doc_versions already uses for version claims. Raised rather than built. ALSO NOT COLLAPSED INTO THIS: the same presentation was reported on 2026-09-14 at v0.60.2 from the latent two-tool surface never promoting, fixed in v0.61.0. Both are live explanations for a report and `grok mcp doctor` distinguishes them in one command.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: reflow2_init.py stops resolving the harness name `grok` to `claude`. Grok is its own entry in HARNESSES with its own spec writing .grok/config.toml in TOML, carrying --graph-path, --export-to and --shared like every other harness. MCP_CONFIGS gains a `format` key so the framework can express a non-JSON harness at all, and both the apply path and the --check path dispatch on it. The write is surgical: _toml_table_span finds reflow2's own table and replaces only those bytes, because that file is the user's whole Grok config and a parse-and-rewrite would reformat it and drop their comments — the standard library can read TOML and cannot write it. Verified end to end on this box: after reflow2_init.py --harness grok, `grok mcp list` printed the server. Four tests in test_init.py asserted the old belief and were rewritten to assert the measurement; a fifth was added for preserving somebody else's servers and comments, and a sixth assertion banning the whole .grok directory came off for the same reason it came off .claude.
